{{nihongo|'''Akunami Shrine'''|飽波神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Suruga Province]].

=== Overview ===
[[File:Akunami jinja 1.jpg|thumb|200px|“Akunami Shrine Mikoshi Procession” around Taishō 10 (1921)<ref name="fujieda">*Photographic Collection: Meiji, Taishō, Shōwa Fujieda*, Furusato no Omoide 75, by Yagi Yōkō and Nomoto Kan’ichi, Tosho Kankōkai, 1980 (Shōwa 55), held by the National Diet Library, accessed March 22, 2019.</ref>]]
According to shrine tradition, Akunami Shrine was enshrined in the 6th year of Emperor Nintoku (318) as the guardian deity of Akunami-go (the entire Shida Plain). It is said that pure water once sprang forth from around small stones at the foot of the mountain and was efficacious for various illnesses, and the shrine was revered as Kawaseki Daimyōjin, a deity who protected people from flooding of the {{ill|Seto river|Q11566620|qid=Q11566620|lt=Seto River}}.

In addition to the annual festival, a grand festival (the Fujieda Grand Festival) is held every three years, bustling with fourteen festival floats (dashi).

The sacred precincts of Akunami Shrine have been selected as one of Shizuoka Prefecture’s “Hometown Forests (Shrine Forests and Temple Forests)” Top 100.

=== History ===
[[File:Engishiki cropped Engishiki Vol 2 Flame 69.jpg|thumb|200px|Volume 9 of the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}, which records “Akunami Shrine”<ref>{{ill|Masamune Atsuo|Q3297160|qid=Q3297160}} (ed.), *Engishiki*, Vol. 2, Nihon Koten Zenshū Kankōkai, 1929, p. 129.</ref>]]
Founded in the 6th year of Emperor Nintoku (318).

In the 3rd year of Eiroku (1560) during the {{ill|Sengoku period|Q204023|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period}}, the {{ill|Takeda clan|Q1210114|qid=Q1210114|lt=Takeda forces}} invaded and burned the shrine buildings and old records. However, the shrine priest Sone Hikohachi Sadaya safeguarded the sacred object, escaped the calamity, and built a small shrine to enshrine it.

In the 5th year of Shōtoku (1715) in the Edo period, the shrine buildings were reconstructed.

In 1873 (Meiji 6), it was ranked as a {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Gōsha}}. In 1907 (Meiji 40), it was designated as a shrine to receive offerings.

In 1931 (Shōwa 6), the worship hall was constructed by parishioners and devotees, and ritual implements and komainu guardian statues were donated.

=== Subsidiary and auxiliary shrines ===
Two shrines are located within the precincts:
* Kanayama Shrine
* Nanatsumori Shrine

=== Japan Heritage ===
On June 19, 2020 (Reiwa 2), the “Dedication Dance of the Akunami Shrine Grand Festival,” together with a group of {{ill|Cultural Property (Japan)|Q858308|qid=Q858308}} around {{ill|Fujieda-juku|Q3069558|qid=Q3069558}}—including “{{ill|Tanaka Castle|Q2970753|qid=Q2970753}} and the Tanaka Castle Honmaru Turret (Historic Site: Tanaka Castle Ruins),” the “Eternal Pine of {{ill|Daikei-ji Temple (Fujieda)|Q43594322|qid=Q43594322|lt=Daikeiji Temple}},” “{{ill|Seto dyed rice|Q106702187|qid=Q106702187}},” and the “Tōkaidō Pine Avenue (Kami-Aoshima Area)”—was recognized as one of the constituent cultural properties of the {{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|Q1009519|qid=Q1009519}}’s {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Cultural Property Protection System}} designation {{ill|Japan Heritage|Q18382798|qid=Q18382798}}, under the story “The First ‘Travel Boom’ in Japan Sparked by Yaji-san and Kita-san: A Journey through Sunshū—A Guidebook to Tōkaidō Travel (Dōchūki) as Depicted in Comic Fiction and Ukiyo-e.”<ref>[https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story094/index.html STORY #094: The First ‘Travel Boom’ in Japan Sparked by Yaji-san and Kita-san, a Journey through Sunshū] (Japan Heritage Portal Site, Agency for Cultural Affairs)</ref><ref>[https://www.city.fujieda.shizuoka.jp/soshiki/sports_bunka/kaidobunka/oshirase/14964.html Recognized as Japan Heritage in Fiscal Year Reiwa 2] (Fujieda City)</ref>.
